1.w: I [am] a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.

2.w: Like a lily among the thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

3.w: Like an apple tree among the trees of the woods, so [is] my beloved among the sons; in his shade I have delighted and sat down, and his fruit [is] sweet to my palate.

4.w: He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me [was] love.

5.w: Sustain me with raisin-cakes, refresh me with apples—for I [am] sick with love.

6.w: His left hand [is] under my head, and his right hand embraces me.

7.w: I adjure you⁺, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field—do not arouse or awaken love, until it pleases.

8.w: The voice of my beloved! Behold, this one is coming, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.

9.w: My beloved [is] being like to a gazelle, or to a young stag of the deer. Behold, this one is standing behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattices.

10.w: My beloved answered and said to me, “Rise up, my my darling, my beautiful one, come away yourself!

11.w: For, behold, the winter has passed by; the rain has passed; it has gone itself.

12.w: The blossoms have appeared in the land, the time of singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land;

13.w: the fig tree puts forth her green figs, and the vines [in] blossom have given forth the fragrance. Arise, come my darling, my beautiful one, and come away yourself!”

14.w: O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice [is] sweet and your appearance [is] lovely.

15.w: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes ruining the vineyards, and our vineyards [are] in blossom.

16.w: My beloved [is] unto me and I unto him; he is grazing among the lilies.

17.w: Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, may you turn and be likened yourself, my beloved, to a gazelle or to a young stag of the deer, upon the mountains of Bether.
